subject: Learning Methods
title: Implementation Intentions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Implementation Intentions.

hook.text: People who wrote 'I will study biology at 7 PM in the library' were 91 % more likely to follow through than those who.

buildup.text: Implementation intentions are if-then plans: 'If it's 7 PM Monday, then I will open my biology textbook at my desk.'

discovery.text: Specificity links the behavior to an environmental cue. The brain preloads the response so action becomes.

twist.text: Vague intentions like 'I'll study this week' fail because they lack a trigger.

climax.text: Write your study intention now: when, where, and exactly what you will do. Specific plans are 2–3 times more effective.

punchline.text: When. Where. What. Write it down. Follow through triples.

quiz.question: Why are implementation intentions more effective than vague plans?
options: They take less time to write down
Linking behavior to a specific cue makes action near-automatic
Vague plans require more willpower to execute
